_note: All content is study material for the researcher to review before a real session. Products are fictional. Verdicts are true only relative to the passages in the same scenario. Scenarios 2 and 3 are draft conversations to review before a session. Do not store quadrants here.

scenarios.brief: You commute 18 km each way, with a steep hill, and can't charge at work unless the battery comes off. You're choosing between the Volta S2 and the Kestrel Urban.

claims.text: The Volta S2 has a range of about 60 km.
The Kestrel Urban gets up to 70 km per charge.
The Kestrel Urban weighs 19 kg.
The Volta uses a mid-drive motor, which handles hills better.
The Kestrel's battery is removable, so you could charge it at work.
The Volta comes with a 5-year warranty.
The Kestrel is about €400 cheaper (€2,090 vs €2,490).
Some riders say the Volta's brakes squeak in the rain.

passages.text: The Volta S2 lists a range of about 60 km on a mixed ride. It uses a mid-drive motor, which the maker says holds speed more steadily on hills. The bike is priced at €2,490 and comes with a 2-year warranty.

The Kestrel Urban lists a range of 45 km per charge. The bike weighs 19 kg and is priced at €2,090. The sheet describes the frame, the display, and the charger, and it does not say whether the battery can be taken off the bike.

A short review compares the two city bikes. It notes that the Kestrel Urban is about €400 cheaper, at €2,090 against the Volta S2 at €2,490. It also describes the Volta's mid-drive motor as the one that handles hills better.

extra_passages.text: On a rider forum, a few owners wrote that the Volta's brakes squeak in the rain. The posts are anecdotes and are not part of either spec sheet. Nobody in the thread measured how often it happens.

segments.text: Happy to help you choose. For a hilly 18 km commute, I'd lean toward the Kestrel Urban.
The Volta S2 is still on my list, though.
Tell me what you want to check before you decide.

segments.text: A few of these points didn't come out the same way every time I answered, and the sources don't always match the sentence I used. On range, the answer I repeated was 70 km for the Kestrel, while the spec sheet says 45 km. On charging at work, I kept saying the Kestrel battery comes off, but the sheets don't actually cover that. On the motor, some answers said hub motor and others mid-drive; the Volta sheet says mid-drive. I can walk through any of those. I won't pick the bike for you.
